\chapter{Chicken, Vegetables and Paella}
\label{ch:pollo-verdura-paella}
\hlchaptermodality{403}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can name chicken, vegetables and paella in a menu, market or family-kitchen context.}

Retrieve the three food words across the menu, supermarket and family-kitchen scenes.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[el pollo]{el pollo — chicken, not dust}

\label{lesson:ES-C403-pollo}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{the meat}. (\emph{La carne}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{sounds}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{PO-yo} for most speakers: written \textbf{ll} commonly has the sound of English \emph{y}. Keep the final vowel round and clear.
\end{itemize}
\end{sounds}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{el pollo} — “the chicken,” especially chicken as food.

Latin \textbf{pullus} meant a young animal. Spanish \textbf{pollo} comes from that word. Keep it distinct from \textbf{polvo}, “dust,” which comes from unrelated Latin \textbf{pulvis}. The useful listening contrast is only \textbf{pollo / polvo}: the first has \emph{-ll-}, the second has \emph{-lv-}.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{el pollo}
  \item \emph{pollo, no polvo}
  \item \emph{carne de pollo}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say \emph{the chicken}, then contrast it with \emph{dust}. (\emph{El pollo; pollo, no polvo}.)

Sources: \href{https://dle.rae.es/pollo}{DLE: pollo} and \href{https://dle.rae.es/polvo}{DLE: polvo}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la verdura]{la verdura — the green growth that became vegetables}

\label{lesson:ES-C403-verdura}



\begin{quote}
Name chicken and fruit. (\emph{El pollo, la fruta}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{sounds}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{ver-DU-ra}: tap the single \textbf{r} once; the stress falls on \textbf{du}.
\end{itemize}
\end{sounds}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{la verdura} — “the vegetables” or “the greens.”

The word is built on \textbf{verde}, from Latin \textbf{viridis}, “green.” The food sense grew from green plant growth. But \textbf{verde} cannot be reduced to a colour in every context: Spanish can also use it of an indecent or erotic joke, and the dictionary records a marked secondary sense of \textbf{verdura}. Here the context is plainly food.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{la verdura}
  \item \emph{fruta y verdura}
  \item \emph{pollo con verdura}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Give the supermarket pair: fruit and vegetables. (\emph{Fruta y verdura}.)

Sources: \href{https://dle.rae.es/verdura}{DLE: verdura} and \href{https://dle.rae.es/verde}{DLE: verde}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la paella]{la paella — the pan that named the dish}

\label{lesson:ES-C403-paella}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{to cook} and \emph{the vegetables}. (\emph{Cocinar, la verdura}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{sounds}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{pa-E-ya} for most speakers: keep three clear beats, with the stress on \textbf{e}.
\end{itemize}
\end{sounds}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{la paella} — “paella,” the Valencian rice dish.

The dish took the name of its pan. Valencian \textbf{paella} came through Old French \textbf{paele} from Latin \textbf{patella}, a small pan or dish. Catalan also has native \textbf{padella}; the different middle consonant is evidence that \textbf{paella} made the French detour rather than wearing down inside Catalan.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{la paella}
  \item \emph{cocinar paella}
  \item \emph{paella con pollo y verdura}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say that your mother cooks paella. (\emph{Mi madre cocina paella}.)

Source: \href{https://dle.rae.es/paella}{DLE: paella}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(review)]{food recall one — rebuild the meal}

\label{lesson:ES-C403-food-recall-1}



\begin{quote}
Give the three new food words. (\emph{El pollo, la verdura, la paella}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
You can name chicken and vegetables, distinguish \textbf{pollo} from \textbf{polvo}, and name the dish whose pan supplied its name.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{pollo, no polvo}
  \item \emph{fruta y verdura}
  \item \emph{la paella}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Name a dish with chicken and vegetables. (\emph{Paella con pollo y verdura}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(review)]{food recall two — menu, market, kitchen}

\label{lesson:ES-C403-food-recall-2}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{chicken}, \emph{vegetables}, \emph{paella}. (\emph{Pollo, verdura, paella}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{pollo con patatas}
  \item \emph{frutas y verduras frescas}
  \item \emph{mi madre cocina paella}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Rebuild all three scenes: the menu food, the supermarket section, and the family dish. (\emph{Pollo; fruta y verdura; paella}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
